newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL MADRID SUFFER SHOCK DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL MADRID SUFFER SHOCK DEFEAT.

text.p: The Spanish championship was ripped wide open on Sunday when leaders Real Madrid crashed 1-0 at Athletic Bilbao.
The defeat reduced their lead over Barcelona to just two points with three games to play.
But Real will take the title if the two finish level on points because of results of games played between them during the season.
Barcelona beat third-placed Deportive Coruna 1-0 on Saturday.

Carlos Garcia gave an inspired Athletic side a well-deserved lead midway through the second half, but Fabio Capello's men nearly snatched a point five minutes from time when Roberto Carlos blasted a superb free-kick against the post.

In a last ditch attempt to equalise, Real goalkeeper Bodo Illgner went forward for a corner but the Real keeper nearly paid the price for his gamble when Athletic broke and narrowly missed scoring a second.
"The league title still depends on what we do," said Raul Gonzalez, who was the only first choice Real striker to play because of the suspension of Pedrag Mijatovic and Davor Suker.
Next weekend Barcelona travel to Hercules, while Real entertain Extremadura, who held champions Atletico Madrid 1-1 on Sunday.
